key_insight: Human teleoperation offers a recovery mechanism for self-driving laboratories, with controller configuration and path guidance shaping operator performance.
engineering_relevance: Adding teleoperation to autonomous lab workflows could help operators resolve unexpected faults without abandoning robotic execution.
method: Controlled a six-DOF UR3e robotic arm using a 3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Pro.
Compared coupled six-DOF velocity control with decoupled translation and rotation.
Evaluated fault recovery and aiming behavior with and without reference-path guidance.
evidence_signal: Across three fault scenarios, comparative trials associated decoupled control with shorter completion times and less rotational motion; a second study found that guidance influenced aiming behavior.
watch_item: The abstract provides no sample sizes or quantitative effect sizes, limiting assessment of robustness and generalizability.
paper_title: Toward Resilient Self-Driving Laboratories through Telerobotic Interventions
